newsitem.title: BULGARIA: POLL SHOWS BULGARIANS BACK TOUGH ECONOMIC REFORMS.
newsitem.headline: POLL SHOWS BULGARIANS BACK TOUGH ECONOMIC REFORMS.

text.p: Almost two thirds of Bulgarians support IMF-prescribed economic reforms carried out by the government, a polling agency said on Monday.

But a survey of 1,300 people by the National Centre for Studying Public Opinion (NCSPO) in July and August shows that some 55 percent do not know the nature of the economic reforms and 64 percent are not familiar with the government's restructuring programme.

"The majority of the Bulgarians are not prepared to face all consequences of the structural reforms as they have no individual strategy for adapting to the new conditions," NCSPO director Asen Yosifov told a news conference.
Bulgaria's government, which took office in May, introduced on July 1 a strict monetary regime known as a currency board, banning the central bank from lending to the government or commercial banks.
The currency board system requires that the amount of levs in circulation be matched exactly by central bank foreign exchange reserves, pegging the lev at 1,000 to the mark.
Prime Minister Ivan Kostov warned earlier this month that the country would face another tough winter but if it got through then steady revival and real development could be expected.

Unemployment is expected to rise drastically as a result of closing loss-making state enterprises and the government plans to get big infrastructure projects under way attracting foreign investments and creating new jobs.

Around half those polled said foreign investments would boost the development of the economy but more than two thirds were against sales of arable land to foreigners and 52 percent opposed sales of Bulgarian firms to foreign companies.
